chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, raising it (to the Imam), said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The olives increase in the water.'
ai.seo_question: What does the hadith about olives increasing in water mean in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) notes that olives increase in water, a statement often interpreted in fiqh regarding the purity of olive oil or the nature of olives themselves in relation to water for purification. This narration is frequently cited by Shia jurists to discuss the physical properties of olives and their oil, particularly in determining whether olive oil is considered pure (tahir) or impure (najis) and how it interacts with water during ritual ablution (wudu). The brevity of the statement invites scholarly debate on whether it refers to the fruit absorbing water or the oil separating, reflecting the practical legal concerns of the early Shia community.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, raising it, said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Olives increase in the water’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ja‘far in a marfu‘ manner who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Olives increase in water.’”
